subject: Creativity
title: The Bauhaus: Where Modern Design Was Born
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Bauhaus: Where Modern Design Was Born.

hook.text: Your IKEA furniture, your smartphone's clean lines, your office building's glass walls — all descend from one school.

buildup.text: Founded in Germany in 1919, the Bauhaus united art, craft, and technology — believing design should serve everyday life.

discovery.text: Its principle: 'Form follows function.' A chair should be comfortable first, beautiful second.

twist.text: The Nazis closed the Bauhaus in 1933, calling it 'degenerate.

climax.text: Apple's design language, minimalist typography, and clean product aesthetics are direct descendants of Bauhaus.

punchline.text: One school, 14 years, permanent impact. The Bauhaus designed the modern world.

quiz.question: What was the Bauhaus's core design principle?
options: Art should be separate from industry

details.summary: The Bauhaus school, founded in 1919 in Weimar Germany, unified art, craft, and technology into a single design philosophy. Its principles of form follows function, minimal ornamentation, and industrial materials shaped everything from architecture to typography to the iPhone.
details.whyItMatters: The Bauhaus invented modern design education and aesthetic philosophy. Nearly every designed object in contemporary life shows its influence, from furniture to digital interfaces.
takeaways: The Bauhaus united fine art with industrial craft and technology
Form follows function became the defining principle of modern design
The school operated only 14 years but influenced a century of design

faq.question: Why was the Bauhaus shut down?
faq.answer: The Nazis closed the Bauhaus in 1933, considering its modernist aesthetic incompatible with their ideology. Faculty members fled to the United States, spreading Bauhaus principles to American design education, particularly through the Illinois Institute of Technology.

faq.question: How does the Bauhaus influence design today?
faq.answer: Minimalist aesthetics, sans-serif typography, modular furniture, and the principle that design should be functional and accessible all trace directly to Bauhaus philosophy. Apple's design language is often cited as contemporary Bauhaus-influenced design.
